newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil strikes deal on Banerj debts.
newsitem.headline: Brazil strikes deal on Banerj debts.

text.p: The Brazilian government has struck a deal with the state of Rio de Janeiro to cover some of the debts of the Banco do Estado de Rio de Janeiro, Finance Ministry executive secretary Pedro Parente said.
Parente told reporters federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal would lend Banerj 2.95 billion reais.

He said 2.05 billion reais would cover debts to employee funds and the other 900 million would be put into a fund to cover "eventual labilities" and act as "security" for potential buyers of the bank.
The deal must still be approved by the Rio de Janeiro state legislature and by the Senate in Brasilia.

If accepted, the Caixa Economica loan would be included in a deal to refinance Rio de Janeiro state's 11 billion reais debt at interest rates of 7.0 percent a year, adjusted for inflation, with a 30-year maturity.
Banerj's sale was postponed twice last year due to court rulings against the privatization. But weak investor interest has also been an obstacle, analysts say.
